neighbours.label: the decimal point in the upper bound of a confidence interval written 'X to Y.ZZ' in epidemiology results
fire: Obesity increased the risk of diabetes (odds ratio 2.31, 95% confidence interval 1.64 to 3.27).
The hazard ratio for death was 1.75 (95% CI 1.20 to 2.55) among smokers.
Patients on the drug were more likely to recover (risk ratio 1.48, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.96).
Night shift work was associated with breast cancer (OR 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.08 to 1.71).
Children in day care had more infections (relative risk 1.90, 95% CI 1.31 to 2.76; P < 0.01).
The adjusted odds ratio was 3.12 (95% confidence interval 1.85 to 5.26) for heavy drinkers.
Women had a higher rate of migraine (rate ratio 2.05, 95% CI 1.44 to 2.92).
Low vitamin D predicted falls (hazard ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.15 to 2.17) in older adults.
quiet: Obesity increased the risk of diabetes in the study, especially among older adults.
The mean age at death was 71.4 years among smokers in the cohort.
Patients on the drug were more likely to recover, according to the authors.
Night shift work was associated with breast cancer in a 2019 review (n = 1,204).
Children in day care had more infections (P < 0.01) during their first winter.
Heavy drinkers made up 12.5% of the sample and were mostly men.
Women had a higher rate of migraine, which the authors linked to hormones.
Low vitamin D predicted falls in older adults (Br J Gen Pract 2011;61:15-20).

notes: Card flags gate-closed (-x- echo 87%). Probe: 'confidence interval 1.21 to 3.04' 1.06, '95% CI 1.10 to 5.25' 0.61 (peak '.'), but hyphenated '0.55-0.93' 0.05; other decimals (54.3 years, 3.50 to 4.75 dollars, version 2.3) ~0.02. Fire items all use 'to' with an upper bound > 1.
